title_en: What space motion sickness is and who gets it
text_en: Changes in gravity can bring on motion sickness and disorientation, and most astronauts become motion sick at some point in flight. Whether a person gets sick in cars, boats or planes on Earth does not predict how sick they will be in space.
text_ko: 중력이 달라지면 멀미가 나고 방향 감각이 흐트러질 수 있으며, 우주비행사 대부분은 비행 중에 멀미를 겪는다. 지구에서 차나 배, 비행기를 탈 때 멀미를 하는지 여부로는 우주에서 멀미가 얼마나 심할지 예측할 수 없다.

sources.title: Risk of Altered Sensorimotor and Vestibular Function
Evidence Report: Risk of Altered Sensorimotor/Vestibular Function Impacting Critical Mission Tasks
OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome

numbers: The challenge risk page says 'the majority' of astronauts and gives no percentage (NASA HRP risk page, 2025). Other NASA documents differ: 50% of women and 38% of men at transition to weightlessness on space station missions, and 67% of first-time flyers on early Shuttle flights (HRP Evidence Report, 2022); 'up to 73%' in the first 2-3 days (OCHMO-MTB-004, 2025).
do_not_claim: Do not give a single percentage for how many crew are affected; the sources differ. Do not say that first-time flyers are more, or less, affected than repeat flyers: the HRP evidence report and the OCHMO briefs disagree.

title_en: Why weightlessness causes motion sickness
text_en: The cause of space motion sickness is not known for certain. The most widely accepted explanation is a sensory mismatch: in weightlessness, information from the eyes, the inner ear, and the senses of body position and touch no longer matches the patterns the brain learned under gravity.
text_ko: 우주 멀미의 원인은 아직 확실히 밝혀지지 않았다. 가장 널리 받아들여지는 설명은 감각 불일치다. 무중력에서는 눈과 속귀(내이), 몸의 위치 감각, 촉각에서 들어오는 정보가 뇌가 중력 아래에서 익혀 온 양상과 맞지 않게 된다는 것이다.

sources.title: OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome
Evidence Report: Risk of Altered Sensorimotor/Vestibular Function Impacting Critical Mission Tasks

do_not_claim: Do not present sensory mismatch as proven, and do not say the shift of body fluid alone causes the sickness; the evidence report says the exact mechanism remains unknown.

title_en: How space motion sickness feels
text_en: Space motion sickness does not always feel like motion sickness on Earth. Feeling generally unwell, losing appetite and lacking the drive to start tasks are nearly universal, often with headache, drowsiness and an uneasy awareness of the stomach, and vomiting can come suddenly with little or no nausea beforehand.
text_ko: 우주 멀미는 지구에서 겪는 멀미와 느낌이 다를 수 있다. 몸이 찌뿌둥하고 입맛이 없으며 일을 시작할 의욕이 나지 않는 증상은 거의 누구에게나 나타나고, 두통과 졸음, 속이 거북한 느낌이 함께 오는 일이 많다. 구토는 메스꺼움이 거의 없다가 갑자기 나올 수도 있다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Altered Sensorimotor/Vestibular Function Impacting Critical Mission Tasks
OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome

do_not_claim: Do not say that sweating or paleness is, or is not, a feature in flight: the OCHMO brief lists both as common symptoms and the HRP evidence report calls them uncommon in flight. Do not treat the absence of nausea as ruling the condition out.

title_en: Limiting head movement
text_en: Head and whole-body movements can start or worsen space motion sickness, and nodding the head forward and back is reported as the most provoking. Limiting head movement and activity, closing the eyes for a while, or concentrating on a task can ease the symptoms.
text_ko: 머리나 온몸을 움직이면 우주 멀미가 시작되거나 심해질 수 있으며, 고개를 앞뒤로 끄덕이는 움직임이 증상을 가장 잘 일으키는 것으로 보고된다. 머리 움직임과 활동을 줄이거나, 잠시 눈을 감거나, 한 가지 작업에 집중하면 증상이 가라앉을 수 있다.

sources.title: OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome
Evidence Report: Risk of Altered Sensorimotor/Vestibular Function Impacting Critical Mission Tasks

title_en: Warmth, smells and air movement
text_en: Being too warm, bad smells, unpleasant sights and certain foods can start or worsen space motion sickness, as can losing a clear visual sense of which way is up. More air movement is one of the listed non-drug measures, so a cooler spot with moving air may help.
text_ko: 너무 덥거나, 나쁜 냄새를 맡거나, 불쾌한 것을 보거나, 특정 음식을 먹으면 우주 멀미가 시작되거나 심해질 수 있고, 어느 쪽이 위인지 알려 주는 시각적 기준을 잃어도 마찬가지다. 공기 흐름을 늘리는 것은 약을 쓰지 않는 대처법의 하나이므로, 덥지 않고 공기가 잘 도는 곳에 있으면 도움이 될 수 있다.

sources.title: OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome

title_en: Keeping up fluids
text_en: Nausea, vomiting and poor appetite in the first days reduce how much a person eats and drinks, while the shift of body fluid toward the head dulls thirst and briefly increases urine output. Keeping up fluid intake is therefore one of the listed non-drug measures, even when there is little urge to drink.
text_ko: 비행 첫 며칠은 메스꺼움과 구토, 입맛 저하로 먹고 마시는 양이 줄어드는 데다, 체액이 머리 쪽으로 쏠리면서 갈증을 덜 느끼고 소변량이 일시적으로 늘어난다. 그래서 물 생각이 별로 나지 않더라도 수분을 꾸준히 섭취하는 것이 약을 쓰지 않는 대처법의 하나로 꼽힌다.

sources.title: OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome

do_not_claim: Do not state an amount to drink; the notes give none. Do not name or recommend any medicine.

title_en: Motion sickness when gravity returns
text_en: After landing, when gravity returns, motion sickness can start again within minutes or on first standing up, even in people who had little of it in weightlessness. Heat and head movements tend to worsen it and limiting activity early on helps. Most cases clear in two to three days.
text_ko: 착륙해서 중력이 돌아오면 몇 분 안에, 또는 처음 일어설 때 멀미가 다시 시작될 수 있으며, 무중력에서 멀미가 거의 없던 사람도 예외가 아니다. 더위와 머리 움직임은 증상을 악화시키는 경향이 있고 착륙 직후에 활동을 줄이면 도움이 된다. 대부분은 이삼일 안에 가라앉는다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Altered Sensorimotor/Vestibular Function Impacting Critical Mission Tasks
OCHMO-TB-010 Rev A: Sensorimotor Overview
OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome
Risk of Altered Sensorimotor and Vestibular Function

numbers: After Shuttle flights (241 crew, 1981-1999): 32% reported vertigo, 14.7% nausea and 8% vomiting; in Russian reports about 11% of people with little or no in-flight sickness had it after landing (HRP Evidence Report, 2022). Most readaptation sickness clears in 2-3 days (OCHMO-MTB-004, 2025).
do_not_claim: The data are from returns to Earth gravity; do not state rates for the Mars surface. Feeling faint on standing up is a separate problem and should not be explained as motion sickness.

title_en: How long it lasts and what to count
text_en: A mild case of space motion sickness brings a few symptoms, sometimes only with head movement, at most a single episode of vomiting and no effect on work, and usually clears within about two days; a moderate case clears by about the third day. Counting vomiting episodes and days since onset helps show which course it is following.
text_ko: 우주 멀미가 경증일 때는 증상이 몇 가지에 그치고 머리를 움직일 때만 나타나기도 하며, 구토는 많아야 한 번이고 업무에 지장이 없으며, 대개 이틀쯤이면 가라앉는다. 중등도일 때도 사흘쯤이면 가라앉는 것이 보통이다. 구토 횟수와 증상이 시작된 뒤 지난 날수를 세어 두면 경과를 가늠하는 데 도움이 된다.

sources.title: OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome

numbers: Severity grading (OCHMO-MTB-004, 2025; table from Barratt et al., 2019): mild - gone in 36-48 hours, at most one retching or vomiting episode, no operational impact; moderate - gone in 72 hours, no more than two vomiting episodes, minimal operational impact; severe - more than two vomiting episodes, visible performance drop, may last beyond 72 hours.

title_en: Symptoms before demanding tasks
title_ko: 중요한 작업을 앞두고 있을 때의 증상
text_en: A crew member who is motion sick may struggle with mission tasks, vehicle controls or a spacewalk, and vomiting inside a spacesuit is dangerous. For this reason spacewalks are not scheduled in the first three days and the first flight days are kept light. Symptoms still present before such a task are worth reporting beforehand.
text_ko: 멀미가 난 승무원은 임무 작업이나 우주선 조종, 선외 활동(우주 유영)을 제대로 해내기 어려울 수 있고, 우주복 안에서 구토하면 위험하다. 그래서 비행 첫 사흘 동안은 선외 활동 일정을 잡지 않고 초반 일정을 가볍게 짠다. 이런 작업을 앞두고 증상이 남아 있으면 미리 알리는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: Risk of Altered Sensorimotor and Vestibular Function
OCHMO-TB-010 Rev A: Sensorimotor Overview
OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome

numbers: Space station flight rule: no spacewalk before 72 hours of mission time; exploration crew scheduling sets aside adaptation time on flight days 1-4 (OCHMO-TB-010, 2023; OCHMO-MTB-004, 2025).

title_en: When to contact the CMO or ground medical staff
title_ko: CMO나 지상 의료진에게 연락해야 할 때
text_en: Contact the crew medical officer (CMO) or ground medical staff if vomiting occurs more than twice, if work performance is visibly dropping, or if symptoms continue beyond about three days. These features belong to the severe grade of space motion sickness, in which fluids given into a vein and a check of blood salts may be considered.
text_ko: 구토가 두 번을 넘거나, 업무 수행이 눈에 띄게 떨어지거나, 증상이 사흘쯤 지나도 이어지면 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 연락한다. 이런 양상은 우주 멀미의 중증 등급에 해당하며, 중증일 때는 정맥으로 수액을 보충하거나 전해질을 확인하는 조치를 고려할 수 있다.

sources.title: OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome

numbers: Severe grade: more than two vomiting episodes, visible performance drop, may last beyond 72 hours (OCHMO-MTB-004, 2025).
do_not_claim: The criteria come from a severity grading table, not from a triage rule tested for a Mars mission; do not present them as a diagnosis. Do not name or recommend any medicine.

title_en: How the body keeps its balance
text_en: Balance depends on the eyes, the inner ear, and position and touch sensors in the muscles and joints. In the inner ear, fluid-filled canals sense head rotation, while two small organs use tiny crystals that shift under gravity to sense head position and straight-line movement.
text_ko: 몸의 균형은 눈과 속귀(내이), 그리고 근육과 관절에서 위치와 촉각을 느끼는 감각기에 의존한다. 속귀에서는 액체가 차 있는 반고리관이 머리의 회전을 감지하고, 다른 두 개의 작은 기관은 중력에 따라 움직이는 미세한 결정을 이용해 머리의 위치와 직선 방향의 움직임을 감지한다.

sources.title: Balance Disorders
sources.publisher: NIH National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders

title_en: What a wearable can and cannot tell about motion sickness
title_ko: 웨어러블로 멀미에 대해 알 수 있는 것과 없는 것
text_en: No wearable reading has been validated as a sign of space motion sickness. Crew wearables in current studies record things such as movement, sleep, heart activity and skin temperature without tying them to motion sickness, and in ground tests body responses to it differed widely between people. What the person feels and reports remains the guide.
text_ko: 우주 멀미를 나타내는 신호로 검증된 웨어러블 측정값은 없다. 현재 승무원 연구에 쓰이는 웨어러블 기기는 움직임, 수면, 심장 활동, 피부 온도 등을 기록하지만 이를 멀미와 연결 짓지는 않으며, 지상 실험에서는 멀미에 대한 신체 반응이 사람마다 크게 달랐다. 따라서 본인이 느끼고 알리는 증상이 판단의 기준이 된다.

sources.title: Ongoing HRP Research in Space
Bio-Monitor
The stability of individual patterns of autonomic responses to motion sickness stimulation (Cowings, Naifeh & Toscano)

do_not_claim: Do not say that heart rate, heart-rate variability, skin conductance, skin temperature, sleep or activity indicates, detects or rules out space motion sickness. The person-to-person finding is from the abstract of a ground laboratory study (58 subjects); the notes contain no measurement made during actual sickness in flight.

title_en: What SANS is
text_en: In long periods of weightlessness, blood and the fluid around the brain and spinal cord shift toward the head. This can lead to swelling of the optic nerve, folds in the retina and flattening of the back of the eye, a group of changes known as spaceflight associated neuro-ocular syndrome (SANS).
text_ko: 무중력 상태가 오래 이어지면 혈액과 뇌척수액이 머리 쪽으로 쏠린다. 그 결과 시신경이 붓고(시신경유두부종), 망막에 주름이 생기고, 눈 뒤쪽이 평평해질 수 있는데, 이런 변화를 묶어 우주 비행과 관련된 신경안구 증후군(SANS)이라고 한다.

key_terms.en: swelling of the optic nerve (optic disc edema)
fluid around the brain and spinal cord (cerebrospinal fluid)

sources.title: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
Hazard: Gravity Fields

title_en: How common and how serious
text_en: Most crew on long missions show at least an early sign of SANS on eye imaging, but only a minority develop swelling that is clinically significant, and the risk is higher on longer missions. Where focus has shifted, vision has so far been correctable with new lenses, and no permanent loss of sharpness has been documented.
text_ko: 장기 임무를 수행한 승무원 대부분은 눈 영상 검사에서 신경안구 증후군(SANS)의 초기 징후를 적어도 하나는 보이지만, 시신경이 임상적으로 의미 있는 정도까지 붓는 경우는 일부에 그치며, 임무가 길수록 위험이 커진다. 초점이 달라진 경우에도 지금까지는 새 렌즈로 시력을 교정할 수 있었고, 시력이 영구적으로 떨어진 사례는 보고되지 않았다.

sources.title: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
OCHMO-MTB-001: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

numbers: About 70% of space station astronauts have some swelling at the back of the eye (NASA HRP risk page, 2025). About 70% of long-duration crew show one or more signs and about 15% develop clinically significant swelling, Frisén grade 1 or higher (HRP Evidence Report, 2022); 18% are diagnosed with clinically concerning SANS (OCHMO-MTB-001, 2024). Every astronaut with a change in refraction was correctable to 20/20 or better (HRP Evidence Report, 2022).
do_not_claim: Do not say the changes are harmless or always reverse: the long-term outcome is unknown and some changes have lasted for years. Do not say it is more common in men; a prospective study found no preference for either sex or eye. The two NASA figures for clinically significant cases (about 15% and 18%) differ, so do not give one as exact.

title_en: Why it happens is not settled
text_en: The cause of SANS is not certain. The leading idea is that the headward shift of fluid in weightlessness congests the veins and may slightly raise pressure inside the skull or let fluid build up where the optic nerve enters the eye, but pressure inside the skull has never been measured directly in flight.
text_ko: 신경안구 증후군(SANS)의 원인은 확실하지 않다. 가장 유력한 설명은 무중력에서 체액이 머리 쪽으로 쏠리면서 정맥에 피가 몰리고, 두개내압(머리뼈 안의 압력)이 약간 오르거나 시신경이 눈으로 들어가는 부위에 체액이 고일 수 있다는 것이다. 다만 비행 중에 두개내압을 직접 측정한 적은 없다.

sources.title: OCHMO-MTB-001: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
SANS Risk Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) Narrative

do_not_claim: Do not say that pressure inside the skull or inside the eye is raised in a given crew member, and do not present any mechanism as proven. Do not say carbon dioxide causes, or does not contribute to, these eye changes: the 2022 HRP evidence report and the 2025 carbon dioxide risk record disagree.

title_en: Stronger spare glasses
text_en: Near vision can drift during a long mission, so glasses in several steps of increasing strength are flown in advance. Changing to a stronger pair when close work becomes blurred manages the blur; it does not treat the underlying change in the eye.
text_ko: 장기 임무 중에는 가까운 것을 보는 시력이 달라질 수 있어, 도수를 단계적으로 높인 안경 여러 벌을 미리 싣고 간다. 가까운 작업을 할 때 흐려 보이면 도수가 더 높은 안경으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있는데, 이는 흐려 보이는 불편을 덜어 줄 뿐 눈 자체의 변화를 치료하는 것은 아니다.

sources.title: OCHMO-MTB-001: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

numbers: The brief says at least three pairs of lenses of increasing power; whether this applies to every crew member is not clear from its wording (OCHMO-MTB-001, 2024).

title_en: No proven way to prevent it yet
text_en: No measure has yet been proven to prevent or reverse SANS. Nutritional supplements and mechanical ways of countering the fluid shift toward the head, such as tight thigh cuffs, are still being studied, so for now they are research rather than self-care.
text_ko: 신경안구 증후군(SANS)을 예방하거나 되돌리는 것으로 검증된 방법은 아직 없다. 영양 보충제나, 허벅지를 조이는 띠처럼 체액이 머리 쪽으로 쏠리는 것을 기계적으로 줄이는 방법이 연구되고 있지만, 지금으로서는 스스로 하는 관리법이 아니라 연구 단계에 있는 방법이다.

sources.title: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
Ongoing HRP Research in Space
OCHMO-MTB-001: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

do_not_claim: Do not recommend supplements, cuffs or any device as prevention or treatment; the studies are listed as ongoing and the notes contain no results.

title_en: Near-vision change is the usual thing noticed
title_ko: 가장 흔히 느끼는 변화는 근거리 시력 변화
text_en: When a crew member with SANS notices anything, it is usually blurred near vision or tired eyes during close work, caused by a shift toward far-sightedness. The eye finds this harder to make up for with age, particularly after about forty. A change in near vision is worth mentioning at the next medical check-in.
text_ko: 신경안구 증후군(SANS)이 있는 승무원이 느끼는 변화가 있다면, 대개는 눈이 원시 쪽으로 변하면서 가까운 것이 흐려 보이거나 가까운 작업을 할 때 눈이 피로해지는 것이다. 나이가 들수록, 특히 마흔 무렵 이후에는 눈이 이런 변화를 스스로 보완하기 어려워진다. 가까운 것을 보는 시력이 달라졌다면 다음 의료 상담 때 이야기하는 것이 좋다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

do_not_claim: Do not say that blurred near vision means SANS is present; the same complaint is common with normal ageing of the eye.

title_en: Distorted vision or a blind spot
title_ko: 휘어 보이거나 안 보이는 부분이 생길 때
text_en: Folds near the centre of the retina can make things look distorted or less sharp, and a few crew members with optic nerve swelling have had an enlarged or new blind spot. Such changes are rare; reporting one allows extra eye testing outside the regular schedule.
text_ko: 망막 중심 가까이에 주름이 생기면 사물이 휘어 보이거나 덜 또렷하게 보일 수 있고, 시신경이 부은 승무원 가운데 몇 명은 시야에 보이지 않는 부분(맹점)이 커지거나 새로 생긴 적이 있다. 이런 변화는 드물며, 알리면 정기 일정과 별도로 눈 검사를 추가로 받을 수 있다.

sources.title: OCHMO-MTB-001: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

numbers: Two crew members had enlarged blind spots right after flight and one reported a blind spot in flight that resolved before return; all three had optic disc swelling (OCHMO-MTB-001, 2024; HRP Evidence Report, 2022).

title_en: Recovery after return to Earth
text_en: After return to Earth, optic nerve swelling has generally eased over weeks to months without treatment. In some astronauts, however, it had not fully returned to the pre-flight level a year later, and the change in focus has lasted for years in some long-mission crew. Eye examinations therefore continue after the flight.
text_ko: 지구로 돌아온 뒤에는 부었던 시신경이 대개 치료 없이 몇 주에서 몇 달에 걸쳐 가라앉았다. 그러나 일부 우주비행사는 일 년이 지나도 비행 전 수준으로 완전히 돌아오지 않았고, 장기 임무 승무원 일부는 초점 변화가 여러 해 동안 남았다. 그래서 비행이 끝난 뒤에도 눈 검사를 계속한다.

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
OCHMO-MTB-001: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

numbers: Prospective study of 11 astronauts on six-month missions: retinal-thickness measures were back to about baseline by roughly 90 days after return; in one unusual case swelling in one eye took 20 months to resolve (HRP Evidence Report, 2022).
do_not_claim: The recovery data are from return to Earth; the notes contain nothing on recovery in Mars gravity. Do not promise full recovery.

title_en: Sudden floaters, flashes or a shadow in vision
title_ko: 갑자기 떠다니는 점, 번쩍임, 그림자가 보일 때
text_en: Contact the crew medical officer (CMO) or ground medical staff immediately if many new floaters, flashes of light, or a dark shadow or curtain across part of the vision appear. These are not typical of SANS; they are warning signs of a detached retina, which is treated as a medical emergency.
text_ko: 눈앞에 떠다니는 점이 갑자기 많아지거나, 빛이 번쩍이는 것처럼 보이거나, 시야 한쪽이 그림자나 커튼에 가린 것처럼 어두워지면 즉시 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 연락한다. 이는 신경안구 증후군(SANS)의 전형적인 양상이 아니라 망막박리의 경고 신호이며, 망막박리는 응급 상황으로 다룬다.

sources.title: Retinal Detachment

do_not_claim: The list is general eye-health advice (NIH National Eye Institute), not a spaceflight-specific rule. Do not say these signs are caused by SANS.

title_en: Usually silent: found by eye examinations, not by a wearable
title_ko: 대개 증상이 없어 눈 검사로 발견되며 웨어러블로는 알 수 없다
text_en: SANS often causes no symptoms beyond a change in near vision, and its earliest sign is seen only on imaging of the back of the eye. It is therefore found by scheduled eye examinations, such as vision tests, ultrasound and optical imaging, not by how a person feels. No wearable reading has been validated as a sign of it.
text_ko: 신경안구 증후군(SANS)은 가까운 것을 보는 시력이 달라지는 것 말고는 증상이 없는 경우가 많고, 가장 이른 징후는 눈 뒤쪽을 찍는 영상 검사에서만 확인된다. 그래서 본인의 느낌이 아니라 시력 검사, 초음파 검사, 광학 영상 검사 같은 정기 눈 검사로 발견된다. 이 변화를 나타내는 신호로 검증된 웨어러블 측정값은 없다.

key_terms.en: optical imaging of the eye (optical coherence tomography)

sources.title: Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
OCHMO-MTB-001: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

numbers: Nominal in-flight eye testing on a six-month mission: around flight day 30, flight day 90 and 30 days before return, plus whenever clinically indicated (OCHMO-MTB-001, 2024).
do_not_claim: Do not say that a wearable signal or a symptom check can detect or rule out SANS, and do not say that a vision complaint means SANS is present. Crew with SANS signs do not report the severe headaches or double vision seen with raised pressure in the head on Earth, so a headache should not be presented as a sign of it.

title_en: Normal age-related near-vision change
title_ko: 나이에 따른 정상적인 근거리 시력 변화
text_en: Near vision also declines normally with age as the lens of the eye stiffens, usually from the mid-forties, with trouble seeing up close, holding text farther away and eyestrain. More light, larger print and reading glasses are the usual remedies. A slow change in near vision is therefore not by itself evidence of a spaceflight effect.
text_ko: 가까운 것을 보는 시력은 나이가 들면서 수정체가 딱딱해져 자연스럽게 떨어지며(노안), 대개 사십 대 중반부터 가까운 것이 잘 안 보이고, 글을 멀리 떼어 놓고 보게 되고, 눈이 피로해진다. 이때는 조명을 밝게 하거나 큰 글씨를 쓰거나 돋보기안경을 쓰는 것이 일반적인 대처법이다. 따라서 근거리 시력이 서서히 달라지는 것만으로는 우주 비행의 영향이라고 볼 수 없다.

sources.title: Presbyopia
Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

numbers: Presbyopia is usually noticed after age 45 (NIH National Eye Institute, 2024). The typical deployed crew member is in their late 40s, and the criterion for an excessive shift in focus is +0.75 dioptres or more over a six-month mission, chosen because a change that large would be unlikely on Earth over the same period without disease (HRP Evidence Report, 2022).

title_en: Why carbon dioxide matters in a sealed cabin
title_ko: 밀폐된 선실에서 이산화탄소가 문제가 되는 이유
text_en: People breathe out carbon dioxide all the time. On Earth the open air carries it away, but a sealed spacecraft depends on removal equipment, and when carbon dioxide builds up in the body it can cause headache, breathlessness and fatigue.
text_ko: 사람은 숨을 내쉴 때마다 이산화탄소를 내보낸다. 지구에서는 트인 대기 속으로 흩어지지만 밀폐된 우주선에서는 제거 장치에 의존해야 하며, 이산화탄소가 몸에 쌓이면 두통과 피로가 생기고 숨이 찰 수 있다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-004 Rev D: Carbon Dioxide (CO2)

numbers: Outdoor air is about 0.04% carbon dioxide, about 0.3 mmHg; indoor air on Earth is typically around 0.08-0.1%, 0.6-0.76 mmHg (OCHMO-TB-004, 2026).

title_en: Pockets of exhaled air in weightlessness
text_en: In weightlessness air does not circulate by itself, so exhaled carbon dioxide can collect wherever fans are not moving the air, for example around the face of a sleeping person. Cabin ventilation is designed to prevent such pockets of carbon dioxide and of heat.
text_ko: 무중력에서는 공기가 저절로 순환하지 않아, 환풍기가 공기를 움직여 주지 않는 곳에서는 내쉰 이산화탄소가 고일 수 있으며, 잠든 사람의 얼굴 주위가 그런 예다. 선실의 환기 설비는 이처럼 이산화탄소나 열이 한곳에 고이지 않도록 설계된다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-002 Rev B: Environmental Control & Life Support System (ECLSS)
OCHMO-TB-004 Rev D: Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

numbers: A simulation found that without adequate ventilation the carbon dioxide around a sleeping astronaut's mouth and chin could exceed 9 mmHg within 10 minutes (HRP SANS Evidence Report, 2022, citing Son et al., 2002). This is a simulated no-ventilation case, not a measurement.

title_en: Carbon dioxide is one possible cause of headache among several
title_ko: 이산화탄소는 두통의 여러 원인 가운데 하나
text_en: Carbon dioxide strongly widens the blood vessels of the brain, which is the proposed link between a build-up of this gas and headache. Headache in flight is also tied to the early shift of body fluid toward the head, to motion sickness, loud noise and low oxygen, so the symptom alone does not show the cause.
text_ko: 이산화탄소는 뇌혈관을 강하게 넓히는데, 이것이 이산화탄소가 쌓일 때 두통이 생기는 이유로 제시된다. 그러나 비행 중 두통은 초기에 체액이 머리 쪽으로 쏠리는 현상이나 멀미, 큰 소음, 산소 부족과도 관련이 있으므로, 증상만으로는 원인을 알 수 없다.

sources.title: HSRB CO2 Risk: Risk Record Rev D.1
OCHMO-TB-004 Rev D: Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome
OCHMO-TB-035 Rev C: Acoustics
OCHMO-TB-003 Rev A: Habitable Atmosphere
Risk of Hypoxia
Relationship between carbon dioxide levels and reported headaches on the International Space Station (Law et al.)
sources.publisher: Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine

sources.title: Frequency and Clinical Features of Space Headache… (van Oosterhout et al.)

numbers: Space station expeditions 2-31: each 1 mmHg rise in carbon dioxide doubled the odds of a reported headache, and a 7-day average below 2.5 mmHg was estimated to keep headache risk under 1% (Law et al., 2014, abstract only); the same dataset covered 49 astronauts, 19 of whom reported headaches (OCHMO-TB-004, 2026). Prospective study of 24 astronauts over 3,596 space days: headache was not associated with cabin carbon dioxide (van Oosterhout et al., 2024, abstract only); weekly mean 2.74 +/- 0.38 mmHg in headache weeks versus 2.66 +/- 0.46 mmHg in headache-free weeks (NASA HSRB risk record Rev D.1, 2025).
do_not_claim: Do not say that a given headache is caused by carbon dioxide. Do not say that carbon dioxide at the levels now kept on the space station does, or does not, raise headache risk: an analysis of earlier expeditions found more headache reports at higher levels, a later prospective study found no association, and NASA's 2025 risk record disputes how that later result should be read.

title_en: Airflow where you sleep
text_en: Sleep stations are meant to have airflow that each person can adjust, both for comfort and to stop carbon dioxide from pooling during sleep. Keeping the fan running and the air directed toward the face helps prevent a pocket of exhaled air from forming there.
text_ko: 개인 침실은 각자 공기 흐름을 조절할 수 있도록 설계하는 것이 원칙인데, 이는 쾌적함을 위해서이기도 하고 자는 동안 이산화탄소가 고이는 것을 막기 위해서이기도 하다. 환풍기를 켜 두고 바람이 얼굴 쪽을 향하게 하면 내쉰 공기가 얼굴 주위에 고이는 것을 막는 데 도움이 된다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-002 Rev B: Environmental Control & Life Support System (ECLSS)
Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

title_en: Reporting symptoms so the air can be checked
text_en: Crew are trained before flight to recognise their own symptoms of carbon dioxide exposure, and symptom reports are part of how the gas is monitored. When a crew member develops symptoms, extra readings with a portable monitor are called for, so saying where and when a headache began helps the right spot to be checked.
text_ko: 승무원은 이산화탄소에 노출되었을 때 자신에게 나타나는 증상을 알아차리도록 비행 전에 훈련을 받으며, 승무원의 증상 보고는 이산화탄소를 감시하는 방법의 일부다. 증상이 생기면 휴대용 측정기로 추가 측정을 하게 되어 있으므로, 두통이 언제 어디에서 시작됐는지 알리면 해당 장소의 공기를 확인하는 데 도움이 된다.

sources.title: HSRB CO2 Risk: Risk Record Rev D.1
OCHMO-TB-004 Rev D: Carbon Dioxide (CO2)

title_en: What tends to relieve it
text_en: A headache from carbon dioxide is described as responding poorly to ordinary headache treatment and as usually easing once the level of the gas is reduced, for which crews have procedures. Other headaches in flight are commonly managed with sleep, exercise, fluids and common pain relief.
text_ko: 이산화탄소로 인한 두통은 일반적인 두통 치료에 잘 반응하지 않고 이산화탄소 농도를 낮추면 대개 가라앉는 것으로 알려져 있으며, 승무원에게는 농도를 낮추는 절차가 마련되어 있다. 비행 중에 생기는 다른 두통은 흔히 수면, 운동, 수분 섭취, 일반적인 진통제로 관리한다.

sources.title: HSRB CO2 Risk: Risk Record Rev D.1
OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A: Space Adaptation Sickness and Space Readaptation Syndrome

do_not_claim: Do not say that a headache which fails to respond to pain relief is therefore caused by carbon dioxide, and do not name a medicine. Sources differ on intensity (the risk record calls the characteristic headache severe; the earlier space station dataset recorded mostly moderate headaches), so do not state how severe it is.

title_en: Places and situations to keep in mind
text_en: Settings named as prone to locally raised carbon dioxide are sleep stations and improvised sleeping spots, a fixed work position held for several hours, maintenance behind panels outside the ventilated space, exercise areas, and a failure of removal equipment. Noting whether a headache began in one of these settings is useful information.
text_ko: 이산화탄소 농도가 국소적으로 높아지기 쉬운 장소와 상황으로는 개인 침실과 임시로 마련한 잠자리, 몇 시간씩 한자리에서 하는 작업, 환기되는 공간 바깥인 패널 뒤쪽에서 하는 정비 작업, 운동 구역, 제거 장치의 고장이 꼽힌다. 두통이 이런 상황에서 시작됐는지 적어 두면 유용한 정보가 된다.

sources.title: HSRB CO2 Risk: Risk Record Rev D.1
OCHMO-TB-002 Rev B: Environmental Control & Life Support System (ECLSS)

do_not_claim: Do not say that a headache starting in one of these settings is caused by carbon dioxide; no measurement of the air a person breathes in these places exists in the notes.

title_en: Other symptoms reported alongside
text_en: In crew reports from earlier missions, headaches at raised carbon dioxide came with fatigue, a general unwell feeling and flushing, and at higher levels with poorer sleep and nausea. These reports are anecdotal, and most textbook signs of carbon dioxide poisoning have never been seen in spaceflight, so they are something to note, not proof of the cause.
text_ko: 이전 임무의 승무원 보고를 보면, 이산화탄소 농도가 높을 때의 두통에는 피로, 몸이 찌뿌둥한 느낌, 얼굴이 달아오르는 증상이 따랐고, 농도가 더 높을 때는 잠을 설치거나 메스꺼움이 함께 나타났다. 다만 이는 개별 사례를 모은 보고에 그치고 교과서에 나오는 이산화탄소 중독 증상 대부분은 우주 비행에서 관찰된 적이 없으므로, 이런 동반 증상은 기록해 둘 사항일 뿐 원인의 증거는 아니다.

sources.title: OCHMO-TB-004 Rev D: Carbon Dioxide (CO2)

numbers: Anecdotal associations compiled in a 2010 NASA technical paper and repeated in OCHMO-TB-004 (2026): headaches at about 2.8-4.5 mmHg with fatigue, malaise and flushing; fatigue, malaise, poorer sleep and nausea above 4.5 mmHg; chronic cough, poor sleep, blurred vision and frontal headaches reported at 3.5 mmHg.

title_en: Headache features that need contact at once
text_en: Contact the crew medical officer (CMO) or ground medical staff immediately for a sudden severe headache, a severe headache with fever or a stiff neck, a headache after a head injury, or a headache with confusion, weakness, numbness, double vision, loss of consciousness, convulsions or trouble breathing. This applies whatever the suspected cause.
text_ko: 다음과 같은 두통이 있으면 즉시 CMO나 지상 의료진에게 연락한다. 갑자기 시작된 심한 두통, 열이 나거나 목이 뻣뻣해지는 심한 두통, 머리를 다친 뒤에 생긴 두통, 그리고 두통과 함께 정신이 혼란스럽거나, 팔다리에 힘이 빠지거나 감각이 없어지거나, 사물이 둘로 보이거나, 의식을 잃거나, 경련이 일어나거나, 숨쉬기가 힘들어지는 경우가 여기에 해당한다. 원인이 무엇으로 짐작되든 마찬가지다.

sources.title: Headache
sources.publisher: NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke

do_not_claim: Do not explain away any of these features with carbon dioxide, noise or poor sleep. The list is general-medicine advice (NIH NINDS), not a spaceflight-specific triage rule.

title_en: Headache red flags that build over time
title_ko: 시간을 두고 나타나는 두통의 위험 신호
text_en: In general medicine, some headache patterns are red flags that call for a doctor's review instead of self-care alone: a headache that worsens over days or weeks or changes its pattern, two or more headaches a week, and a new constant headache in a person who did not have headaches before.
text_ko: 일반 의학에서는 두통의 몇 가지 양상을 스스로 돌보는 것만으로 넘기지 말고 의사의 진료를 받아야 하는 위험 신호로 본다. 며칠이나 몇 주에 걸쳐 점점 심해지거나 양상이 달라지는 두통, 일주일에 두 번 이상 생기는 두통, 전에는 두통이 없던 사람에게 새로 생겨 계속되는 두통이 여기에 해당한다.

sources.title: Headache
sources.publisher: NIH National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke

do_not_claim: This is general-medicine advice (NIH NINDS) and was not written for spaceflight, where headaches are common. Sudden, severe or neurological features are covered by the separate contact-at-once paragraph and must not be downgraded to this slower list.

title_en: What cabin readings and wearables cannot show
title_ko: 선실 측정값과 웨어러블로 알 수 없는 것
text_en: The cabin displays the carbon dioxide level and notifies the crew when it is outside safe limits, but that reading does not show what one person breathes: sensors sample fixed points, and no method of measuring the air a person actually inhales is in use. No wearable reading has been validated as a sign of headache from carbon dioxide.
text_ko: 선실에서는 이산화탄소 농도가 표시되고 안전 한계를 벗어나면 승무원에게 알림이 가지만, 이 측정값이 한 사람이 실제로 들이마시는 공기를 보여 주는 것은 아니다. 감지기는 정해진 지점의 공기만 측정하며, 개인이 들이마시는 공기를 직접 측정하는 방법은 쓰이고 있지 않다. 이산화탄소로 인한 두통을 나타내는 신호로 검증된 웨어러블 측정값도 없다.

sources.title: HSRB CO2 Risk: Risk Record Rev D.1
OCHMO-TB-004 Rev D: Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

numbers: Design standard (NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2, requirement V2 6004): 1-hour average carbon dioxide partial pressure not above 3 mmHg (OCHMO-TB-004, 2026). Space station operations: below 5.3 mmHg in the early programme, below 4.0 mmHg from 2010, and a 24-hour average of no more than 3 mmHg since 2016 (NASA HSRB risk record Rev D.1, 2025).
do_not_claim: Do not say that a normal cabin reading rules out a local build-up of carbon dioxide, and do not say that heart rate, skin response, temperature, sleep or activity readings indicate raised carbon dioxide or a headache caused by it.

title_en: What a person can notice about the cabin
title_ko: 선실 환경에서 스스로 느낄 수 있는 것
text_en: Noise, heat, cold and still air are cabin conditions a person can notice directly, and living quarters are meant to be neither too hot, too cold nor too loud. Noise can bring irritation, headaches and poorer sleep even when it does not seem harmful, and comfort differs between people, so local airflow and clothing are meant to be adjustable.
text_ko: 소음, 더위, 추위, 공기가 정체된 느낌은 승무원이 직접 느낄 수 있는 선실 환경이며, 거주 공간은 너무 덥거나 춥거나 시끄럽지 않게 만들어야 한다. 소음은 해롭게 느껴지지 않는 수준이라도 짜증과 두통을 일으키고 잠을 방해할 수 있다. 쾌적하게 느끼는 조건은 사람마다 다르므로 주변 공기 흐름과 옷차림은 각자 조절할 수 있게 하는 것이 원칙이다.

numbers: Cabin air health limits: 18-27 degrees C with 25-75% relative humidity; comfort zone 20-25 degrees C with 30-60% humidity (OCHMO-TB-002, 2023). Outside launch, entry and abort, noise from off-nominal operations must stay below 85 dBA (OCHMO-TB-035, 2023).
do_not_claim: Do not say that a person can sense the carbon dioxide level itself; the notes do not say so. Do not give a single decibel figure for the continuous-noise limits, which are set as frequency-band curves.
